start.title: A Life in Haran
start.text:
You live in Haran with your father Terah, your wife Sarai, and your nephew Lot.
You are seventy-five years old.

choices.text: Live as Abram in Haran, seventy-five years old
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:4 — Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

choices.text: Live as a young man in the city of Ur
choices.feedback: By Genesis 12, Abram had already left Ur and was in Haran, aged seventy-five.

choices.text: Live as king over a great nation
choices.feedback: Genesis does not describe Abram as a king; he was a wandering herdsman.

the_call.title: The Call of the Lord
the_call.text:
The Lord speaks to you.
What does He command?

choices.text: 'Go from your country, your people and your father's household to the land I will show you'
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:1 — The Lord said to Abram, 'Go from your country, your people and your father's household to the land I will show you.'

choices.text: 'Stay in Haran and worship the household idols'
choices.feedback: Genesis says the Lord told Abram to leave, not to stay.

choices.text: 'Build a temple to Me here in Haran'
choices.feedback: The Lord told Abram to go to a land He would show him.

the_promise.title: The Promise
the_promise.text:
The Lord adds His promise.
What does He say?

choices.text: 'I will make you into a great nation and bless you; all peoples on earth will be blessed through you'
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:2-3 — 'I will make you into a great nation, and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you.'

choices.text: 'I will give you great riches to keep to yourself'
choices.feedback: The promise was that all peoples would be blessed through Abram, not that he would hoard riches.

choices.text: 'You will have a long life and no descendants'
choices.feedback: The Lord promised Abram a great nation of descendants.

telling_sarah.title: Your Household
telling_sarah.text:
You must prepare your family for the journey.
Who goes with you?

choices.text: Take Sarai your wife and Lot your nephew
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:5 — Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran.

choices.text: Leave Sarai behind in Haran
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram took Sarai with him.

choices.text: Go alone with only a walking staff
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram took his household, flocks, and possessions.

preparing.title: What You Carry
preparing.text:
You gather what you will take on the journey.
What goes with you?

choices.text: All the possessions and people you have acquired in Haran
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:5 — Abram took all the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran.

choices.text: Only a small bag of bread
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram left with his whole household and possessions.

choices.text: A chariot of gold from the king of Haran
choices.feedback: Genesis does not describe a chariot from any king.

departure.title: You Set Out
departure.text:
The time has come to leave.
Where do you set out for?

choices.text: Set out for the land of Canaan
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:5 — They set out from Haran to go to the land of Canaan, and they arrived there.

choices.text: Set out for Egypt to become rich
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram set out for Canaan; Egypt came later, during a famine.

choices.text: Set out with no destination in mind
choices.feedback: The Lord had a specific land in mind — Canaan.

the_road.title: Into the Land
the_road.text:
You travel through the land of Canaan.
How far do you go?

choices.text: Travel as far as the great tree of Moreh at Shechem
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:6 — Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the great tree of Moreh at Shechem.

choices.text: Turn back to Haran halfway there
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram arrived in Canaan.

choices.text: Cross the sea to a distant island
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram traveled by land into Canaan.

doubt_night.title: The Lord Appears
doubt_night.text:
At Shechem the Lord appears to you.
What does He say?

choices.text: 'To your offspring I will give this land'
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:7 — The Lord appeared to Abram and said, 'To your offspring I will give this land.'

choices.text: 'This land belongs to another people forever'
choices.feedback: The Lord promised the land to Abram's offspring.

choices.text: 'Return to Haran; you were wrong to come'
choices.feedback: The Lord confirmed the promise in Canaan, not sent Abram back.

stargazing.title: At Shechem
stargazing.text: You have heard the promise. What do you do at Shechem?

choices.text: Build an altar there to the Lord who appeared to you
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:7 — Abram built an altar there to the Lord, who had appeared to him.

choices.text: Build a palace of cedar for yourself
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram built an altar, not a palace.

choices.text: Say nothing and move on quickly
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram worshiped by building an altar at Shechem.

canaan_arrival.title: Between Bethel and Ai
canaan_arrival.text:
You move on from Shechem into the hills.
Where do you stop and pitch your tent?

choices.text: Pitch your tent in the hills between Bethel and Ai, and build another altar
choices.feedback: Genesis 12:8 — From there Abram went on toward the hills east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east; there he built an altar and called on the name of the Lord.

choices.text: Pitch your tent in the city of Sodom
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram pitched his tent between Bethel and Ai.

choices.text: Sail back across the river to Haran
choices.feedback: Genesis says Abram continued southward through Canaan.

altar.title: Calling on the Name of the Lord
altar.text:
You call on the name of the Lord at your new altar.
The promise of a great nation goes with you as you journey on toward the Negev.
